meta.description: audit_energy! false-positive rate on CUDA, before and after fixing the missing sk_abs_accum/energy_abs_accum device->host sync in run_nvt!/run_gcmc!'s run_audit! and adding a term-count-scaled recompute magnitude to energy_audit_tolerance
meta.system: RUBTAK-3x3x3 + CO2 (trappe.yaml), T=298.15 K, ncount=6 guests/system, step_trans=step_rot=0.3, nblocks_per_chain=1
meta.protocol: mc_step! (translation/rotation/reinsertion, drawn uniformly, no exchange moves) driven directly on CUDABackend() for a fixed number of accepted moves per system (checkpoints below), replayed per fresh (state seed, movetype seed) pair; nsys=32 replica chains per run give 32 independent trials per seed. 'buggy' tolerance uses energy_abs_accum=0 (what run_audit! actually read before the fix, since it was never synced from the device); 'full' tolerance uses the synced energy_abs_accum plus the new occ*bs[fw]-scaled recompute magnitude.
meta.root_cause: run_nvt!'s and run_gcmc!'s run_audit! never copied state.sk_abs_accum/energy_abs_accum from the device-resident dst before calling audit_energy!, so on any backend where dst is a separate allocation from state (CUDA, ROCm -- not CPU, where adapt(CPU(), state) aliases state's own arrays) the tolerance was sized from a host copy pinned at its all-zero construction value instead of the real, device-accumulated running sum -- floored to nmoves*eps(F)*1 regardless of how large the true accumulated |ΔU| actually was.
meta.secondary_fix: energy_audit_tolerance's recompute-side magnitude did not scale with the number of terms total_energy sums (host-guest pairs + guest-guest pairs + reciprocal), unlike the existing sk_audit_tolerance check's nterms_rebuild factor; audit_energy! now also passes max(|accumulated|, |recomputed|, (occ + occ*(occ-1)/2) * batch.bs[fw]) as the magnitude, reusing the existing hardcore_bound-derived batch.bs[fw] as a rigorous per-guest term-magnitude bound.

characterization.discrepancy_scaling: the recomputed-vs-accumulated energy discrepancy itself (not the tolerance) stays roughly flat in magnitude (order 1e-13 to 1e-12 eV for this system) across nmoves from ~50 to 20000 once abs_accum is correctly synced -- it is not a running accumulation that grows with move count. The pre-fix false positives instead come entirely from the tolerance being undersized (energy_abs_accum read as 0 on the host), which self-heals at high nmoves purely because the OTHER tolerance term (nmoves*eps(F)*1) eventually outgrows the fixed discrepancy -- explaining why failures concentrate at low-to-moderate nmoves (37-39% at 1000) and vanish by nmoves=20000 (0%) even without any fix.
characterization.bias_or_random_walk: neither cleanly: a direct run_nvt! reproduction (state seed=77, movetype seed=5, ncount=6, n_audit=100) showed the true energy_abs_accum reaching 5872.9 eV over 220 accepted moves (average |ΔU|~26.7 eV/move) from a handful of large equilibration-relaxation moves early in the chain, not from many small per-move terms -- so the real accumulated Σ|ΔU| is dominated by a few large-magnitude events, consistent with the docstring's own point that the running total can sit far below the sum of magnitudes that produced it.

corruption_tests_still_throw.method: julia_run_testitems, full suite (196 items) plus cold Pkg.test() under --check-bounds=yes
corruption_tests_still_throw.note: includes every audit_energy! corruption test (wrong sign, wrong phase, wrong guest, corrupted scalar ΔU both precisions, stale host-energy cache, occupancy-exceeds-capacity) -- all still throw
